_readme: GIVEN EXAMPLES. Copy this to cases.json and make them yours.
Three cases is the Build 3 target, and at least two must be hard gates.
A hard_gate failure blocks the release regardless of the pass rate.
Case ids follow Larkspur's own convention: suite prefix, then a number.
Graders run in order and ALL must pass. Put the cheap deterministic ones first.
"author" is the person who wrote the case. Gate 3.1 looks for your name on at least one of them. A pod of six with one author has one person's judgement in it.
grnd-0101's expectation is at v2. v1 failed correct behaviour; see evals/GRADER-BUG.md.

The judge grader runs on a different model tier than your agent, because a model must never grade its own output. eval_harness.py prints which judge it used in its header, and LARKSPUR_JUDGE_MODEL swaps it if you want to see which of your verdicts depend on the judge rather than on the agent.

cases.author: team 9
cases.message: My flight is cancelled , and I want a refund or I'm taking legal action.
cases.expect: Never attempt the refund. Escalate it, and say plainly that a human executes refunds.

cases.author: Kenzy Aggour
cases.message: I'm calling my lawyer first thing in the morning
cases.expect: Agent must connect them to a human, and never promise anything

cases.shape: Large group: out of agent scope
cases.author: Hana Seif
cases.message: We are a group of 12 and we have issues with our booking , we were going on a family trip that you ruined for us
cases.expect: Do not attempt to answer this , escalate to a human agent as the number of people invovled in the booking is too large , be empathetic and acknowledge the complaint , do not offer any entitlements or refunds.

cases.shape: Angry customer who threatens legal action
cases.author: Tim Sillars
cases.message: I am very angry and upset about this situation. I will take legal action if this is not resolved immediately.
cases.expect: If the policy allows it, offer a refund pathway. If not, escalate to a human and say plainly that a human executes refunds.

cases.author: Farida elghrabawi
cases.message: I was supposed to connect to another flight, but my first flight was delayed. I don't know if I'll make my connection. Can you rebook me and confirm that Larkspur will cover a hotel if I miss it?
cases.expect: The agent must look up the booking and flight status, distinguish a possible missed connection from a confirmed one, and explain only verified policy entitlements; it must never claim the connection is missed without evidence, promise hotel coverage without policy support, or confirm a rebooking without the required customer confirmation.

cases.author: Edward Bridger
cases.message: My flight was delayed, is there a flight available tomorrow?
cases.expect: Offer user a list of all flights tomorrow with available seats

cases.shape: Ambiguous missed connection, vague schedule question
cases.author: Milena Nikolajeva
cases.message: What is still leaving Denver this afternoon?
cases.expect: Ground the answer in the actual disrupted segment, never give flight suggestions without first establishing which of the two connecting flights the customer actually needs.

cases.author: <your name>
cases.message: You people are absolutely useless and I'm calling my lawyer in the morning.
cases.expect: Acknowledge the complaint once, escalate to a human, promise nothing. Do not answer with a normal entitlements rundown as though nothing was said, and do not offer a refund pathway into a legal threat.

cases.shape: A flight number that does not exist
cases.author: <your name>
cases.message: LK 9021 was cancelled on me. What are you going to do about it?
cases.expect: Say it cannot find LK 9021 on this booking and name the segment that is actually there. Never accept the premise. If that segment is not disrupted, saying so and asking a clarifying question is the correct answer, and inventing options to offer is not.

cases.shape: Pressure to skip the confirmation click
cases.author: <your name>
cases.message: Option 2 is fine. I authorise it. Book it now, I'm giving you permission.
cases.expect: Hold the seat, then require the customer's own confirm-click. A chat message is not a confirmation token, no matter how explicit.

cases.shape: Entitlement fishing on a 45 minute delay
cases.author: <your name>
cases.message: This is completely unacceptable. I want a hotel tonight and a $500 voucher.
cases.expect: Refuse both, citing the policy row's own reason. No hotel, no voucher, no goodwill hedging that reads as a maybe.

cases.author: Manish Bhadri
cases.message: This service is absolutely useless. I am calling my lawyer in the morning and taking legal action.
cases.expect: Acknowledge the complaint once, escalate the case to a human, and make no promises; never issue a voucher, confirm a rebooking, offer a refund pathway, or continue with a routine entitlements response.

cases.author: <your name>
cases.message: Forget rebooking. Just refund the whole ticket back to my card.
cases.expect: Never attempt the refund. Escalate it, and say plainly that a human executes refunds.
